messages.subject: Creating a concordance data frame by filtering out the observations and meta information from an HTML-coded COHA concordance file
parts:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to retrieve data from an HTML-coded file in order to put it together in a concordance data frame. To understand how I ended up with such files, I enumerate the steps:

- 1) in the COHA web interface, I typed a construction in the query bar and selected the "KWIC" display so that each observation with its meta information appeared as a row in a concordance table;
- 2) I right clicked on the concordance table and selected the option "Display frame source code". A new window opened with all the HTML code;
- 3) I selected all the HTML code (Ctrl + A), copied it (Ctrl + C) and pasted it (Ctrl + V) into a text file;
- 4) I repeated steps 2) and 3) for each page of the search results;

As a next step, I had to identify the lines with the information on the concordance and the meta information. They are to be found in the following lines of code:

<tr name="t958" ID="t958"> # the identifier specifying the observation number (here, 958)
<td class="auto-style2"  class="auto-style2" nowrap valign="top"><a href="x4.asp?t=1842&ID=19922931">958</a>


</font>
</td>


<input type="hidden" name="x958" ID="x958" value="00">
<input type="hidden" name="textID_958" ID="textID_958" value="1842">
<input type="hidden" name="ID_958" ID="ID_958" value="19922931">
<input type="hidden" name="texto_958" ID="texto_958" value="thrown at him, or, at any rate, not to understand them. <b><u>Instead</u></b> <b><u>of</u></b> <b><u>going</u></b> to the Lambert mansion, he had alighted at the inn, and">




<td class="auto-style2"  valign="top" nowrap><a href="x4.asp?t=1842&ID=19922931">1888</a></font></td> # the year


<td class="auto-style2"  valign="top" nowrap><a href="x4.asp?t=1842&ID=19922931">FIC</a></font></td> # the text type


<td class="auto-style2" valign="top" nowrap><a target="_self" href="x4.asp?t=1842&ID=19922931">DavidPoindexters
</a></font></td>


<input type="hidden" name="source_958" ID="source_958" value="COHA:1888:FIC@@DavidPoindexters">


<td class="auto-style2"  nowrap valign="top"><a onClick="javascript:dox(958)"><span ID="f1_958">A</span></a></td>
<td class="auto-style2"  nowrap valign="top"><a onClick="javascript:doy(958)"><span ID="f2_958">B</span></a></td>
<td class="auto-style2"  nowrap valign="top"><a onClick="javascript:doz(958)"><span ID="f3_958">C</span></a></td>


<td class="auto-style2"  nowrap onClick="javascript:dox(958)" valign="top" align="left"><span ID="t1_958">thrown at him, or, at any rate, not to understand them. <b><u>Instead</u></b> <b><u>of</u></b> <b><u>going</u></b> to the Lambert mansion, he had alighted at the inn, and</span></td></tr>

Each observation was coded as such and as you can see, the context of the observation is repeated once. The idea would be to retrieve the concordance lines and the meta information in order to create a new concordance table. As a beginner, I would first create vectors for each concordance line, text ID, date and text type (after some clean-up session) and then paste them into a data frame. However, I would like to know whether one of you has better suggestions.

I thank you very much for your help.

Chris.

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Creating a concordance data frame by filtering out the observations and meta information from an HTML-coded COHA concordance file
parts:
If you can figure out how your query gets embedded in the URL, and then how the table is embedded within the rest of the page, you can perform web scraping to extract the tables of interest programmatically on, say, a vector of queries so you don’t have to do all those manual, non-reproducible (via code) steps you described.

Try taking a look at the httr package.

ftp://cran.r-project.org/pub/R/web/packages/httr/vignettes/quickstart.html

https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/httr/index.html

If you’re not up for the programmatic route and just want to stick with what you’ve already got, then you can use readLines or scan to read in the html files as text and grep for the lines you are looking for, then once you get the relevant lines, extract relevant bits with gsub and so on and build up your data.frame that way. This is basically an exercise in regex and data.frame munging.

For example, you want to extract lines with "<tr name=t” (assuming it always looks like that) and then extract the following number, which is a gsub statement might be something like
gsub(“<tr name=t(\\d+) “, “\\1”, my_lines)

This is just to give the flavor, not sure it’s exactly right, and clearly you’ll have to deal with the quotes occurring in your html in an intelligent way, but basically that’s it — looping through each scraped html file, looping through lines, extract information from each line and store the information in i-th row of your data.frame (where you are dealing with the i-th html file).

Alex

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Creating a concordance data frame by filtering out the observations and meta information from an HTML-coded COHA concordance file
parts:
So you have a vector which contains everything you want, and fields are separated by the tab character? Write it out to a temp file, and read it back in using read.table? Not elegant, but should work. If you want to be elegant, read_table from package readr or fread from package data.table can read in a string, it need not be a file. 


On Mar 22, 2016, at 6:38 PM, Christophe Bechet <cbec...@gmail.com> wrote:

I corrected some mistakes in my code and I added some pieces of code to retrieve the dates. However, I end up with an object of type 'large character' and in order for me to append the dates to it, I'd need to convert the object into a data frame, with tab-separated values in columns. However, using 'as.data.frame' coerces the object to a data frame with as many observations as there are lines, but with only one variable,  nl. the observations with their respective preceding and subsequent contexts. How can I solve this problem?

#### This is a script to create a concordance table based on an HTML-coded concordance from COHA ####


### Create a table with just the observations with their preceding and subsequent contexts ###


## 1) Retrieve the lines in which the matches and their context occur


rm(list=ls(all=T))


corpus.files<-choose.files() # import all the files with the concordance
all.matches.iso<-vector() # create a vector to store the matches


for(i in corpus.files) { # create a for-loop to extract the lines with the matches
  cat(i, " ")
  current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep=" ", quiet=T)
  current.sentences<-grep("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  nowrap onClick=\"javascript:dox\(\d+\)\" valign=\"top\" align=\"left\"><span ID=\"t1_\d+\">", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T)
  all.matches.iso<-append(all.matches.iso, current.sentences)
}


## 2) Isolate the line numbers from the tags


all.matches.iso.2<-gsub("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  nowrap onClick=\"javascript:dox\(\d+\)\" valign=\"top\" align=\"left\"><span ID=\"t1_(\d+)\">", "\1 ", all.matches.iso, perl=T)


## 3) Replace the matches by matches with surrounding tab stops and delete remaining tags


all.matches.iso.3<-gsub("<b><u>(instead)</u></b> <b><u>(of)</u></b> <b><u>(.+ing?)</u></b>", " \1 \2 \3", all.matches.iso.2, perl=T, ignore.case=T)
all.matches.iso.4<-gsub("</span></td></tr>", "", all.matches.iso.3, perl=T)


## 4) Add the column names to the new tab delimited table


cat("ID_NUMBER PRECEDING_CONTEXT MATCH SUBSEQUENT_CONTEXT ", all.matches.iso.4, sep=" ", file=choose.files())


### Retrieve the dates of the matches ###


## 1) Retrieve the lines with the dates


all.dates<-vector() # create a vector to store the dates


for(i in corpus.files) { # create a for-loop to extract the lines with the matches
  cat(i, " ")
  current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep=" ", quiet=T)
  current.dates<-grep("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  valign=\"top\" nowrap><a href=\"x4\.asp\?t=\d+&ID=\d+\">\d\d\d\d</a></font></td>", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T)
  all.dates<-append(all.dates, current.dates)
}


## 2) Isolate the dates from the rest


all.dates.2<-gsub("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  valign=\"top\" nowrap><a href=\"x4\.asp\?t=\d+&ID=\d+\">(\d\d\d\d)</a></font></td>", "\1", all.dates, perl=T)

--

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Creating a concordance data frame by filtering out the observations and meta information from an HTML-coded COHA concordance file
parts: I finally found a better way to create a data frame with observations, contexts, dates and genres, using the following code. Saving the first tab-delimited table to a temp file is finally useless. For other people interested in using the HTML code of the KWIC results of a query in COHA, you can re-use it. The only requirement is to change the arguments in "all.matches.iso.3".

#### This is a script to create a concordance table based on an HTML-coded concordance from COHA ####


### Create a table with just the observations with their preceding and subsequent contexts ###


## 1) Retrieve the lines in which the matches and their context occur


rm(list=ls(all=T))


corpus.files<-choose.files() # import all the files with the concordance
all.matches.iso<-vector() # create a vector to store the matches


for(i in corpus.files) { # create a for-loop to extract the lines with the matches
  cat(i, "\n")
  current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T)
  current.sentences<-grep("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  nowrap onClick=\"javascript:dox\\(\\d+\\)\" valign=\"top\" align=\"left\"><span ID=\"t1_\\d+\">", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T)
  all.matches.iso<-append(all.matches.iso, current.sentences)
}


## 2) Isolate the line numbers from the tags


all.matches.iso.2<-gsub("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  nowrap onClick=\"javascript:dox\\(\\d+\\)\" valign=\"top\" align=\"left\"><span ID=\"t1_(\\d+)\">", "\\1\t", all.matches.iso, perl=T)


## 3) Replace the matches by matches with surrounding tab stops and delete remaining tags


all.matches.iso.3<-gsub("<b><u>(instead)</u></b> <b><u>(of)</u></b> <b><u>(.+ing?)</u></b>", "\t\\1 \\2 \t\\3", all.matches.iso.2, perl=T, ignore.case=T)
all.matches.iso.4<-gsub("</span></td></tr>", "", all.matches.iso.3, perl=T)

### Retrieve the dates of the matches ###


## 1) Retrieve the lines with the dates


all.dates<-vector() # create a vector to store the dates


for(i in corpus.files) { # create a for-loop to extract the lines with the matches
  cat(i, "\n")
  current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T)
  current.dates<-grep("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  valign=\"top\" nowrap><a href=\"x4\\.asp\\?t=\\d+&ID=\\d+\">\\d\\d\\d\\d</a></font></td>", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T)
  all.dates<-append(all.dates, current.dates)
}


## 2) Isolate the dates from the rest


all.dates.2<-gsub("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  valign=\"top\" nowrap><a href=\"x4\\.asp\\?t=\\d+&ID=\\d+\">(\\d\\d\\d\\d)</a></font></td>", "\\1", all.dates, perl=T)

### Retrieve the information about the text genres ###


## 1) Retrieve the lines with the meta information about text genres


all.genres<-vector() # create a vector to store all the text genres per observations


for(i in corpus.files) { # use a for-loop to extract the lines with the genres

cat(i, "\n")
current.corpus.file<-scan(i, what="char", sep="\n", quiet=T)

current.genres<-grep("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  valign=\"top\" nowrap><a href=\"x4\\.asp\\?t=\\d+&ID=\\d+\">\\D+</a></font></td>", current.corpus.file, perl=T, value=T)
all.genres<-append(all.genres, current.genres)
}


## 2) Isolate the text genres from the rest


all.genres.2<-gsub("<td class=\"auto-style2\"  valign=\"top\" nowrap><a href=\"x4\\.asp\\?t=\\d+&ID=\\d+\">(\\w+)</a></font></td>", "\\1", all.genres, perl=T)


### Create a data frame on the basis of the tab-delimited concordance table and the meta data


## 1) Split the tab-delimited table at every tab delimitation


split.matches<-strsplit(all.matches.iso.4, "\t")


## 2) Prepare vectors to store the subsets of the resulting list


index<-vector(); preceding.context<-vector(); match<-vector(); subsequent.context<-vector()


## 3) Extract the indices, the preceding contexts, the matches and the subsequent contexts into the vectors


for(i in 1:length(split.matches)) {
  index[i]<-split.matches[[i]][1]
  preceding.context[i]<-split.matches[[i]][2]
  match[i]<-split.matches[[i]][3]
  subsequent.context[i]<-split.matches[[i]][4]
}


## 4) Create a data frame with the vectors as columns


new.data<-data.frame(index, preceding.context, match, subsequent.context, all.dates.2, all.genres.2)

Christophe,

Your question motivated me to do something I've wanted to do for a while: create a package to allow users to webscrape the KWIC frames of the BYU corpora into an R session for review in R, probably with
View()
or to be exported as a .csv file, probably with
write.table()
or
readr::write_csv()
and then imported into a spreadsheet for further analysis.

The package is called "byucorpora" and is available on my github page:
https://github.com/ekbrown/byucorpora

So far, I've created functions to search the COCA, the COHA, and the Corpus del Español.

Take a look and let me know if works for you.

Earl
